newsitem.title: POLAND: Head of ING Bank's Polish unit resigns.
newsitem.headline: Head of ING Bank's Polish unit resigns.

text.p: Stan Szczurek, General Manager of ING Bank NV Warsaw said on Tuesday he was resigning from his post from July 1 to become the president of telecommunications firm Netia Telekom.

ING said in a statement that Szczurek, who has managed ING's Warsaw branch for four years, oversaw its establishment as a leading foreign bank operating in Poland and helped ING acquire a majority stake in Poland's Bank Slaski SA.
Szczurek told Reuters in a telephone interview he saw the new job as a challenge similar to the launch of a foreign banking operation at the onset of Poland's market reforms.
"In a way I have decided that I will not be able to do much more for ING in Poland," he said.
"I am moving to a telecoms company...which in a few years may play a similar role for the Polish market and consumers as the first Western bankers have played for the banking industry," he added.
ING said it would soon announce Szczurek's successor.

Netia Telekom S.A., established in 1996, is a joint venture of the Polish-US company R.P. Telekom SA, Swedish firm Telia AB and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development. It is developing several local telephone networks in Poland.
